reconcile.note: Clarke reads John's single mention of Mary Magdalene as selective focus, while the Synoptics report additional women at the tomb.

discrepancy.note: Paine contrasts Luke's several named women with John's Mary Magdalene alone, taking the mismatch as evidence the resurrection accounts do not agree.

quotes.text: Luke says it was Mary Magdalene and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women… and John states that Mary Magdalene came alone. So well do they agree about their first evidence!
quotes.attr: Thomas Paine (d. 1809), The Age of Reason, Part II.

quotes.text: …if it is difficult to call in question the tradition of the three synoptical Gospels, according to which many women came to the tomb, it is certain, on the other hand, that in the two most authentic accounts which we possess of the resurrection, Mary of Magdala plays her part alone.
quotes.attr: Ernest Renan (d. 1892), The Apostles (Eng. transl., 1866), ch. I.

sides.snippet: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
sides.verseText: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.

sides.snippet: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw the stone taken away from the tomb.
sides.verseText: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw the stone taken away from the tomb.
